source.title: Astraios: Parameter-Efficient Instruction Tuning Code Large Language Models
source.authors: Terry Yue Zhuo; A. Zebaze; Nitchakarn Suppattarachai; Leandro von Werra; Harm de Vries; Qian Liu; Niklas Muennighoff

record.tranche_reason: The study measures loss across model sizes and instruction-tuning steps, reports a small-to-large loss prediction claim, and shows that scaling outcomes can depend on the tuning method and learning rate. It does not fit pretraining power laws or test compute-optimal allocations.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the study's own instruction-tuning loss scaling, small-to-large loss prediction, and loss/downstream-performance correlations. The downstream task, robustness, and security results are not rows because they do not themselves measure the claimed loss-scaling behavior. Loss curves provide no tabulated numerical values.
record.test_reason: New setting for the claim: instruction tuning of StarCoder 1B–16B with FFT and six PEFT methods. It reports final train and test loss across model size and training steps, and how downstream tasks change with size. It fits no power law and tests no compute-optimal allocation. Appendix F argues, against Kaplan, that the learning-rate choice matters for scaling. That bears on V7, but the main contribution is the new-setting result, so T3 rather than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add four points. Downstream gains from size are mixed: generation tasks improve, comprehension tasks show inverse-scaling-like patterns. Larger models are less robust and produce more insecure code. The small-to-large loss claim rests on consistent ranking of methods, not a fitted law. The authors note a proper scaling law would need over 100 models.
record.recipe_differences: This study examines instruction-tuning loss for code models across model sizes, PEFT methods, and training steps; it does not reproduce the original pretraining power-law fits or compute-optimal allocation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Loss trajectories vary by tuning method and training duration. Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA size trends change with learning-rate choice; P-Tuning is described as unstable; (IA)3 loss changes are insignificant.

fits_no_version.finding: The ranking of tuning methods by final loss stays consistent across 1B–16B. Authors say small-model loss can be 'a useful predictor' for larger models.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Relative loss ordering of fine-tuning methods transfers across model scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Final instruction-tuning loss correlates with mean downstream score across methods. The correlation is strong overall (test loss rs .9579) but near zero or negative at 1B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning loss on general instruction data predicts downstream task performance.

record.problems: The authors state that experiments used a single run, limiting reliability and exposing results to experiment noise. Loss values are presented in plots rather than tables; no power-law fit is performed; data scaling is not tested; and the study says that a scaling law would ideally use more than 100 models.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. Per-task downstream scores and robustness/security results are outside the measured loss-scaling outcomes cataloged here.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss and no power-law fit.
All: no fitted law extrapolated, no forecast error, size range about one order of magnitude.
All: no fixed-compute allocation; data scaling explicitly not studied.
Power-law form, which is never fitted (only monotonic decrease over 4 sizes). Data scaling. Other modalities, repeated data, transfer.
Prediction from pretraining loss; any quantified prediction of downstream score from scale.
Fitted exponents, parameter counting, compute-optimal fitting method.

missing.what: Downstream Pass@1 versus model size for generation tasks, per method
Inverse scaling of defect and clone detection with model size, per method
1-shot demonstrations flatten defect-detection inverse scaling; LoRA and FFT clone detection rises to 7B then falls at 16B
Correlation between updated-parameter count and final loss (overall test-loss τ .3598)

record.verdict_notes: Single run per configuration. Sizes are base-model sizes, while updated parameters range from about 0.25M to 15.5B. The reader's 'challenges' label for V7 from R14/R15 was inverted: LR-dependent reversal is the setup dependence V7 predicts. The reader's V9/V7 validation issue is resolved by unlinking R9–R12 from V7. Robustness (RC@1 grows with size) and security results are different constructs and are not recorded.

versions.untested_parts: The study measures instruction-tuning loss, not held-out pretraining loss, and does not fit power laws in parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No quantified forecast error is reported; the size range is 1B to 16B, and the study does not test predictions across several orders of magnitude.
No fixed-compute-budget comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is tested; data scaling is explicitly not studied.
The study does not vary architecture depth, width, or other architecture details.
The study tests instruction-tuning loss trends for code models only; it does not fit or establish the same power-law form, and it does not test other modalities, repeated data, or transfer.
The study tests correlations between instruction-tuning loss and aggregate downstream scores for its code models, not downstream predictability from pretraining loss across general language models.
The study tests variation across PEFT methods and learning-rate choices, but not alternative parameter-counting conventions, compute-optimal fitting methods, or pretraining schedules.

relationships.condition: Instruction tuning with FFT and six PEFT methods at the main learning rates, StarCoder 1B–16B
relationships.reason: Text says train and test loss 'strictly decrease' with size for all seven methods (R1–R7). FFT loss keeps falling with steps (R11). Re-tuned Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA also decrease (R16, R17). Power-law form is not fitted.
relationships.display_finding: Training and test loss decreased with size across all seven methods, full fine-tuning improved with steps, and retuned Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA also improved, without a power-law fit.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Instruction tuning with FFT and six PEFT methods at the main learning rates, StarCoder 1B–16B
source_check.reason: R1–R7, R11, R16 and R17 report decreasing loss, without establishing the power-law form required by V5. Appendix J explicitly leaves a proper scaling law for further work.

relationships.reason: (IA)3 loss changes are insignificant (R9). P-Tuning is non-monotonic and unstable (R10). PEFT methods show no clear continued decrease, unlike FFT (R8, R12).
relationships.display_finding: (IA)3 loss changes were insignificant and P-Tuning was unstable and non-monotonic, while full fine-tuning showed continued loss reduction.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R9 reports insignificant changes and R10 reports non-monotonicity after an initial decrease. These method-specific exceptions qualify a decreasing power-law extension across PEFT training duration; they do not establish the form elsewhere.

relationships.condition: Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA at the initial learning rate, 1B–3B
relationships.reason: Final loss increases with model size under the initial LR (R14, R15). The decrease returns only after raising the LR (R16, R17), so the size trend depends on LR choice.
relationships.display_finding: Final loss increased with model size at the initial learning rate, but decreased after the learning rate was raised.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA at the initial learning rate, 1B–3B
source_check.reason: R14 and R15 explicitly report increasing loss with model size in this condition group, reversing the decreasing relationship required by V5. Recovery in separately retuned conditions does not change that verdict.

relationships.condition: Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA, 1B and 3B, learning rate varied
relationships.reason: The direction of the size trend flips with learning rate (R14, R15 vs R16, R17). Authors say LR schedule 'may matter a lot', unlike Kaplan.
relationships.display_finding: Changing learning rate reverses the direction of the size trend between 1B and 3B models for Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA.

source_check.condition: Prompt Tuning and AdaLoRA, 1B and 3B, learning rate varied
source_check.reason: R14–R17 establish learning-rate dependence of a qualitative size trend. They estimate neither fitted exponents nor compute-optimal allocations and do not demonstrate curvature away from a fitted single power law.

relationships.display_finding: Pass@1 generally increased with size, including full-fine-tuning Python synthesis scores from 16.95 to 38.47.

labels.reason: Section 4 explicitly describes inverse-scaling-like comprehension results. Table 2 gives P-Tuning defect accuracy of 53.70 at 1B and 11.00 at 16B; intermediate results and clone detection are non-monotonic.

relation.reason: The study directly measures loss and downstream performance across model sizes and training duration, including conditions with absent or reversed expected trends.

tranche.reason: Beyond introducing instruction tuning as a new setting, Appendix F explicitly argues for learning-rate qualifications to prior scaling conclusions; loss reversals and inverse-scaling-like downstream results require qualification of the claims.

source_check.notes: No fitted power laws or compute-optimal allocations are reported, and Appendix J acknowledges single runs. Appendix F's Prompt Tuning is distinct from the main suite's P-Tuning.
